适用前提.observed_input_and_state:
In the uncompressed branch, the old code allocates metadata according to uncompressed_size but bounds the available input only with remaining_bytes derived from compressed_size, then calls memcpy(mp, p, bytes_avail). When the declared compressed size is greater than the uncompressed size, and a read truncated by the remaining input still leaves bytes_avail greater than metadata_bytes, the copy goes beyond the destination buffer; the subsequent size_t subtraction of metadata_bytes underflows. The original 4 MiB check constrains only the allocation size and cannot ensure that the copy length is no greater than the destination's remaining capacity; checking metadata_bytes == 0 after the copy also cannot prevent the overrun. For example, sizes of 16 and 8 can trigger it when 16 bytes are copied in the first round.
Current review type description: heap-buffer out-of-bounds write (CWE-122), with unsigned underflow of the remaining-capacity counter

安全反证.repair_observed_not_proof_of_any_other_c:
The fix establishes three constraints in sequence: if the two declared sizes of an uncompressed entry differ, it returns ARCHIVE_FATAL before allocation and reading; if compressed_size exceeds 4 MiB, it returns ARCHIVE_WARN; after entering the uncompressed copy branch, it also limits bytes_avail to metadata_bytes. The last condition directly ensures that the copy length does not exceed the remaining destination capacity, keeping subsequent capacity subtraction and pointer advancement within the allocation boundary. The compressed-size limit constrains input scale, while size consistency and pre-copy capacity truncation jointly address the original overrun mechanism.
Current review fix mechanism description: When input remaining bytes and target remaining capacity come from different length fields, first validate the field relationship required by the encoding mode, then constrain the write length simultaneously by input remaining bytes and target remaining capacity; limit the operation before copying, subtracting capacity, and advancing the pointer.
